summary: St. Kitts and Nevis has unusually good official fiscal data on CBI: the Federal budget estimates carry a 'Citizenship by Investment' revenue line (actual, budget and in-year projection) every year, and the Director of Audit's reports give audited CIU collections 2016-2024 with breakdowns; IMF Article IV vintages give CBI revenue as % of GDP for 2010-2026, with revisions driven partly by GDP rebasing. Revenue rose from EC$175m (2016) to a peak of EC$669m (2022), then collapsed after the 2023 reforms (EC$244m Jan-Aug 2024; a projected EC$124m in 2025 against a EC$495m budget). Application counts exist only via the EU (1,987 in 2023, 223 in 2024); the CIU publishes no annual report despite a legal duty since 2024, and off-budget flows (real estate, SIDF before ~2018, and post-August-2024 statutory Unit accounts) are poorly documented.

events.title: Citizenship-by-investment program launched
events.description: St. Kitts and Nevis launched the world's first CBI program, the year after independence.
events.quote: In 1984, St. Kitts and Nevis launched its Citizenship-by-Investment Program

events.title: Sugar Industry Diversification Foundation (SIDF) established
events.description: SIDF created as an independent foundation funded by CBI contributions after the closure of the sugar industry; became the main donation route.
events.quote: the SIDF was established in 2006 as an independent foundation, funded by contributions from the ECP

events.title: US FinCEN advisory on abuse of the St. Kitts and Nevis CBI program
events.description: FinCEN warned US financial institutions that illicit actors, including OFAC-designated Iranian nationals, obtained SKN passports through the program.
events.quote: certain foreign individuals are abusing the Citizenship-by-Investment program

events.title: Canada imposes visa requirement on St. Kitts and Nevis citizens
events.description: Canada removed the visa exemption (SOR/2014-267, registered 21 Nov 2014, in force noon ET the next day), citing risks from the CBI program.
events.quote: Failure to satisfy the criteria is due in large part to risks stemming from the country's Citizenship-by-Investment Program.

events.title: First CBI dividend paid to citizens
events.description: New government paid a 'CBI dividend' to Social Security contributors; the 2024 budget said it reached about 17,500 people in the first round. IMF later urged forgoing such payments.
events.quote: The CBI dividend payment alone impacted about 17,500 individuals in its inaugural round.

events.title: New CBI regime: Board of Governors, Technical Committee; SGF limited-time offer
events.description: Board of Governors and Technical Committee from 1 Jan 2023; SGF contribution cut to US$125,000 for 1 Jan-30 Jun 2023.
events.quote: Effective January 1, 2023 , St. Kitts and Nevis will move to appoint a Professional Citizenship by Investment (CBI) Board of Governors.

events.title: US-Caribbean roundtable agrees six CBI principles
events.description: Five Eastern Caribbean CBI states and the US Treasury agreed principles incl. interviews, FIU checks, independent audits, and suspension of Russian and Belarusian applicants.
events.quote: In February 2023, our Federation hosted the Historic US-Caribbean Roundtable on CBIs at the Park Hyatt.

events.title: Prices roughly doubled; SISC replaces SGF; mandatory interviews
events.description: S.R.O. 26 of 2023: minimum SISC US$250,000 (single), real estate US$400,000, private homes US$400,000/800,000; interviews mandatory; agents regulated.
events.quote: [Published 27th July 2023, Extra Ordinary Gazette No. 44 of 2023]

events.title: Nationals of six countries excluded from CBI
events.description: Exclusion Order bars citizens and residents of Russia, Belarus, North Korea, Afghanistan, Iraq and Iran.
events.quote: every citizen of, and persons ordinarily resident in, the following countries shall be excluded

events.title: Canada partially lifts visa requirement
events.description: SKN nationals holding a Canadian visa in the past 10 years or a current US non-immigrant visa may use an eTA instead of a visa.
events.quote: the visa requirement imposed on nationals of St. Kitts and Nevis in 2014 has been partially lifted

events.title: Regional Memorandum of Agreement sets US$200,000 minimum
events.description: Five ECCU CBI countries signed an MoA setting a common minimum price of US$200,000 and shared standards, after consultations with the EU.
events.location: PDF p. 64 (printed p. 60), Annex IX para 2
events.quote: the ECCU countries signed a regional Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) in March 2024, including setting the minimum pricing of US$200,000

events.title: Citizenship by Investment Unit Act passed
events.description: CIU to become a statutory body corporate with its own Board; SISC paid directly into the Consolidated Fund; annual report required by 31 October.
events.quote: Passed by the National Assembly this 14th day of June, 2024.

events.title: Family-of-four price cut to US$250,000
events.description: S.R.O. 20 of 2024: SISC US$250,000 covers a main applicant or family of up to four (was US$350,000).
events.quote: US$250,000 (Two Hundred and Fifty Thousand United States Dollars) for a main applicant or a family with up to four total persons

events.title: CIU closed as a government department
events.description: The National Audit Office states the CIU as a department closed on 9 Aug 2024; CBI revenue in the 2024 public accounts covers 1 Jan-8 Aug only. The 2025 budget address dates the statutory Unit's restructuring to 1 October.
events.quote: The Citizenship by Investment Unit, as a department of the government, was closed with effect from August 9th 2024.

events.title: PM says CBI revenue fell ~60% and visa-free access was at risk
events.description: PM Drew reported CBI revenue of EC$218m to September 2024 vs EC$620m in 2023 and said the country had been on the brink of losing EU/UK visa-free access.
events.quote: Saint Kitts and Nevis was on the brink of losing that precious visa-free access.

events.title: 'Prison project' claim against previous administration
events.description: In 2024 the Prime Minister claimed a real-estate project under the previous government produced 'tens of thousands' of citizenships; a political claim, not independently verified.
events.quote: The ill-conceived Team Unity Prison Project had resulted in tens of thousands of citizenships being issued from a single venture

events.title: Real estate minimum cut to US$325,000
events.description: S.R.O. 43 of 2024 cut approved-development real estate to US$325,000 and single-family private homes to US$600,000.
events.quote: [Published 25 th October 2024, Extra-Ordinary Gazette No. 66 of 2024]

events.title: 13 investors deprived of citizenship; agents blacklisted
events.description: Deprivation of Citizenship Order 2025 for investors who paid below statutory minimums; RIF Trust blacklisted, Latitude suspended (later reinstated per the report).
events.quote: failed to pay the statutory minimum investment required

events.title: Regional CBI regulator notified to the EU
events.description: The five Eastern Caribbean CBI countries jointly notified the European Commission of a regional regulator (with residency requirement and biometrics).
events.quote: In August 2025, the five Caribbean countries jointly notified the Commission of the establishment of a regional regulator

events.title: CIU announces genuine-link requirement and move away from contribution routes in 2026
events.description: Chairman's update says citizenship will require a genuine link and the programme will begin transitioning from contribution-based pathways in 2026.
events.quote: Looking ahead to 2026, the Programme will commence its transition away from contribution-based pathways.

events.title: FinCEN advisory rescinded
events.description: The CIU says FinCEN formally removed advisory FIN-2014-A004 on 24 February 2026.
events.quote: The advisory, which had been in place since 2014, was formally removed on 24 February 2026

events.title: Statutory Citizenship Unit begins operating; government claims record revenue
events.description: The 2025 budget address dates the CIU restructuring into a statutory body to 1 October 2024 and claims record-breaking revenue since; EU data show only 223 applications in all of 2024.
events.quote: increased applications, and record-breaking revenue since the restructuring on 1 October

events.title: Budget: CBI shortfall drives revenue miss
events.description: 2026 budget address: non-tax revenue 48.3% below budget due to a CBI slowdown (figures match 2024), and 2025 revenue projected ~31.3% below budget largely because of CBI receipts.
events.quote: approximately 31.3 percent largely attributable to the shortfall in receipts from the CBI Programme.

programs.name: St. Kitts and Nevis Citizenship by Investment Programme
programs.notes: Oldest CBI program. Routes over time: SIDF donation (from 2006), Hurricane Relief Fund (c. 2017-2018), Sustainable Growth Fund (to July 2023), Sustainable Island State Contribution (from 27 July 2023), approved real estate, private homes, public benefit option, alternative investment options (2020-2023). CIU became a statutory body in 2024.

new_indicators.name: CBI inflows to an off-budget development fund, share of GDP
new_indicators.definition: CBI contributions paid to a national development fund outside the budget (e.g. St. Kitts SIDF) divided by GDP
new_indicators.notes: Not included in cbi_fiscal_revenue when the fund is off-budget

new_indicators.name: CBI inflows recorded in the capital account, share of GDP
new_indicators.definition: CBI-related inflows recorded in the balance-of-payments capital account (as defined by the IMF source) divided by GDP
new_indicators.notes: Distinct from budgetary CBI fees recorded as services exports
